_tuning_notes: Nile crocodile in swamps. Neutral on land, ambush predator in water: lunge_range is the scan radius in blocks, grab_ticks the drag duration (40 = 2s with two chews at half attack each). Not tamable, not breedable (no items set). Phase 3: diet.hunts doubles as cage-trap bait (item form of the prey). RARITY: tier 'uncommon' supplies the spawn weight; group_size and nearby_cap are pinned here (1-2, cap 4). nearby_cap denies natural spawns when that many of this animal are already within 64 blocks — the fix for persistent CREATURE mobs accumulating forever. ECOLOGY 0.4.2: Nile crocodiles are a river animal; the species was swamp-only and raw-id, so it saw no rivers and no Terralith biome at all. BABY SIZE 0.4.2: baby_scale moved 0.5 -> 1.0. The client already bakes the baby mesh through vanilla's BabyModelTransform (body halved, head full size) and vanilla age scaling halves the hitbox, so a 0.5 here was a SECOND shrink and calves rendered at a quarter of adult size. 1.0 = vanilla baby proportions. TERRALITH PASS: Terralith's ice_marsh joins #c:is_swamp; a Nile crocodile under ice is excluded for the same reason as frozen rivers. SIZE PASS 0.4.6: scale set against MEASURED vanilla hitboxes rather than by eye (cow 0.90x1.40, horse 1.40x1.60, polar bear 1.40x1.40, ravager 1.95x2.20, wolf 0.60x0.85, turtle 1.20x0.40, ocelot 0.60x0.70, chicken 0.40x0.70). Attributes.SCALE is uniform and multiplies the MODEL and the HITBOX together, so this is the one lever that cannot desync them. 0.95x ravager width, 1.85x turtle height: long and low. SIZE PASS revised: the first attempt scaled an already-wrong box. Measuring the baked meshes showed the hitboxes never matched the models — the hippo mesh was 1.06 blocks tall inside a 1.60 box (66% fill, a third of it empty air), while the gorilla mesh was LARGER than its hitbox (121%). Builder dimensions in MenagerieEntities now match the measured mesh, and this scale multiplies model and hitbox together from there, so the drawn animal fills the box it is struck in.
guide_blurb: The river is its dinner table. Stay off the tablecloth.
